chunks: By Allāh, it never occurred to me, and I never imagined, that after the Prophet the Arabs would snatch away the caliphate from his Ahlu’l-bayt (the members of his house), nor that they would take it away from me after him, but I suddenly noticed people surrounding the man to swear him allegiance.

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ: the People of his House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْعَرَبَ: the Arabs (specifically the Quraysh and companions in this context)
key_terms.يَخْطُرُ بِبَالِي: to cross one's mind or imagination
key_terms.يُبَايِعُونَهُ: they were swearing allegiance to him

ai.seo_question: What was Imam Ali's reaction to the rapid transfer of power after the Prophet's death?
ai.summary: This passage from the letter to Malik al-Ashtar captures Imam Ali’s (AS) personal astonishment at the rapid political shift, highlighting the disconnect between the Prophet's household and the broader Arab community regarding succession. It underscores the Shia perspective that the Imamate was a divine designation often overlooked by the masses, who quickly pledged allegiance to others while Ali remained focused on spiritual and administrative duties.
